newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BIS says report on Brazil's real incorrect.
newsitem.headline: BIS says report on Brazil's real incorrect.

text.p: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said a report in Jornal do Brasil about the value of Brazil's real currency was incorrect.
BIS said the newspaper, which reported the Bank as saying Brazil's real was 20 percent overvalued against the dollar, had inaccurately quoted from its annual report released on Monday.
But the BIS annual report only made a factual observation about the movement in the real, and gave no value judgement about the real, a BIS spokesman said.

"Brazil's Real plan introduced in mid-1994 has also sought to reduce inflation through greater exchange rate stability supported by tight monetary policy. Given that the exchange rate tended to appreciate initially and, since early 1995, has depreciated at a slow and gradual rate somewhat below that of consumer price inflation, a real appreciation of 20 percent has taken place since mid-1994."
